Mostly yes. The flow we agreed is built, committed and pushed. Your earlier paste shows the page running. But I haven't clicked through it in a browser myself. And with real laser data it has only run in tests and in a script on dev data, never on your screen.

**What you can navigate now:**
- **Shell and jobs:** shell, *Calibrate on* (defaults to N−1), *Validate on* (optional).
- **Live errors as soon as a job is read:** whole-shell plan, the camera table, and each camera's detail with its bushing rings and a **Label bushings ↗** link.
- **Opening images:** click a cell, a ring, **Laser captures** or **Bushings**. ←/→ to step, S/L/R for the layers, zoom and pan.
- **Weight and Captures sliders:** the ✓ marks move with the Captures slider. Then **Refine**, a **Live / Refined** toggle, earlier refines of the job, and **Errors on** calibration or validation job.
- **Upload:** **What the refine changes** → **Upload refined calibration…**
- **Import backfilled laser observations:** this is how GEV's Job‑35 gets laser data.

**What hasn't been seen working yet:**
- **The import and a GEV refine.** Restart the dev server first, since the server code changed after your last start. Then import `obs_dw35.matched.jsonl` on M7B2 47.3 DW and pick Job‑35‑DW. That's the first time laser errors, ✓ marks and Refine run on GEV data.
- **The validation view on real data.** No dev shell has two jobs with observations, so it has only run in tests. It will work on GEV once both DW jobs have data: Job‑35 backfilled, and anything after 22:33 UTC today stored by laser-mask.

**Not built:** the bushing-image timeline (collections → runs, scrubbing, predictions on unlabeled images, choosing the fit and verification image sets). Bushings still come from each camera's current `report.json`.

Restart:
```
cd /home/user/work/repositories/app && yarn dev
```

If the import or the GEV plan misbehaves, paste the page or the server log line and I'll fix it.

**I think the best is the official `even-terminal`, the one you already have installed.** For most features, a third-party option is at best on par with it, and every one of them adds risk. They're mostly a few weeks old, have one maintainer, and many have never been tested on real glasses. The official tool is maintained by Even, it's the only one built specifically for Terminal Mode, and it already runs on Linux with Tailscale. Its `even-terminal claude` wrapper also puts a session you run in your own terminal onto the glasses.

Your setup does have one gap. You mostly use Claude Code in the **VS Code extension**, and the official tool can't see those sessions. It only sees sessions it starts itself or ones you launch through `even-terminal claude` in a terminal. So the best third-party option depends on what you want to fix:

- **To see your VS Code sessions on the glasses, use [g2-claude-remote](https://github.com/ThatCrispyToast/g2-claude-remote).** It follows Claude Remote Control sessions from the desktop app, the CLI and VS Code. It runs on Linux and sends nothing to anyone but Anthropic. The catch is that it's built on a reverse-engineered, unofficial Claude API, so it may break the terms of service and could stop working with any Claude update.
- **To get a cleaner view of sessions you already run in tmux, use [glancecode](https://github.com/sousyllc/glancecode).** It's the most careful design here: it binds to localhost only, uses local voice, and reads each approval back before pressing anything. The catch is that it's had no commits since 09-21 and has 2★.

I wouldn't pick terminal-mode-console, even though it's the most capable alternative. Its own README admits to open CORS and remote-code-execution exposure, and you'd be running it on your work machine.

What I'd do: use the official tool for a week with `even-terminal claude` in a terminal. Try g2-claude-remote only if you really miss seeing your VS Code sessions.

You're right, and I was wrong. The official tool can see your VS Code sessions. I've now read its code: it lists sessions with the Claude Agent SDK's `listSessions`, which reads every saved session in `~/.claude/projects` (VS Code, CLI or anything else on this machine). When you pick one and talk to it, it resumes that session through the SDK ([claude/provider.js:128](../.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.1/lib/node_modules/@evenrealities/even-terminal/dist/claude/provider.js#L128), [claude/session.js:263](../.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.1/lib/node_modules/@evenrealities/even-terminal/dist/claude/session.js#L263)).

That removes the main reason I gave for g2-claude-remote. There's no gap for it to fill, so I'd drop it, unofficial API included. **The official tool is the clear pick**, and none of the third-party tools adds anything you need.

One thing I haven't checked: when you continue a VS Code session from the glasses, the SDK runs that turn in a separate process. The open VS Code panel probably won't show those new turns until you reopen the session. If you reply in VS Code and on the glasses at the same moment, the two may end up as separate branches of the conversation. If you see that happen, it's the cause, not a bug in your setup.

The choice worked: you picked **Choice A**, and it came back to me as your answer.

So when I ask you a multiple-choice question, Terminal Mode shows it on the glasses, you pick with the ring, and I carry on. That's the same path tool approvals take.
